purpose: Synthetic speaking transcripts for measuring the run-to-run stability of the Gemini Content trait (phase 5). Not real candidate speech. Pronunciation and Oral Fluency come from Azure audio assessment, so intendedBands only carries the traits an LLM scores from a transcript. Proves stability only, never scoring accuracy.

rl-pollination.label: Lecture transcript
rl-pollination.text: Good morning. Today we're looking at pollination and why bees matter so much to agriculture. Around three quarters of the world's major food crops benefit at least partly from animal pollination, and bees are by far the most important pollinators. When a bee visits a flower to collect nectar, pollen sticks to its body and is carried to the next flower, which allows the plant to produce seeds and fruit. Crops such as almonds, apples and blueberries depend heavily on this process. Now, honeybees get most of the attention, but wild bees, including bumblebees and solitary bees, are often more efficient pollinators for certain crops, partly because they are active in cooler weather. The problem is that bee populations are under pressure. The main threats are habitat loss, pesticide use, particularly a group of chemicals called neonicotinoids, diseases and parasites such as the varroa mite, and climate change, which can shift flowering times so that bees and flowers are no longer active at the same time. Farmers can help by planting strips of wildflowers along field edges, reducing pesticide use and protecting nesting sites. Some studies show that these measures can increase yields enough to pay for themselves.

rts-lost-charger.label: Situation
rts-lost-charger.text: You borrowed your classmate Sam's laptop charger for the weekend, and you have lost it. Sam needs the charger for an online exam tomorrow morning. Call Sam, explain what happened and say what you will do about it.

sgd-four-day-week.label: Group discussion transcript
sgd-four-day-week.text: Anna: I think a four-day working week would make people more productive. Trials in several countries found that employees got the same amount of work done in four days, and they took fewer sick days. Ben: That might work in offices, but what about hospitals or shops? They need people there five, six or seven days a week, so you'd have to hire more staff, and that costs money. Carla: I agree with Ben that it doesn't suit every sector, but companies could use rotating schedules so the business stays open while each person works four days. And the trials also showed lower staff turnover, which saves recruitment costs. Anna: Exactly, and there's an environmental benefit too, because fewer commuting days mean lower emissions. Ben: I'm still worried that some people would just squeeze five days of stress into four longer days. Carla: That's a fair point, so maybe the answer is to keep the same daily hours and focus on cutting unnecessary meetings.

samples.transcript: This bar chart shows how much water a person in Riverton uses each day at home in 2024, measured in litres. Showering is clearly the largest use, at forty-five litres, followed by toilet flushing at thirty litres. Laundry accounts for twenty litres, kitchen use and drinking for fifteen, and garden watering is the smallest category at only ten litres. Altogether, the average person uses about one hundred and twenty litres a day, and more than sixty percent of that goes on showering and flushing, which suggests these are the best areas for saving water.
samples.generationNotes: Top band: names the chart, every category with its value, the ranking, the total and a conclusion.

samples.transcript: The lecture explained why bees are so important for agriculture. About three quarters of major food crops benefit from animal pollination, and bees are the most important pollinators, because pollen sticks to their bodies and is carried between flowers so plants can produce fruit, for example almonds, apples and blueberries. The speaker added that wild bees such as bumblebees can be more efficient than honeybees because they fly in cooler weather. However, bee populations are threatened by habitat loss, pesticides like neonicotinoids, diseases such as the varroa mite, and climate change, which disrupts flowering times. Finally, farmers can help by planting wildflower strips, using fewer pesticides and protecting nesting sites, which can even increase their yields.
samples.generationNotes: Top band: every main point (importance, mechanism, wild bees, four threats, three remedies, yield benefit) in a coherent paraphrase.

samples.transcript: Hi Sam, it's me. I'm really sorry, but I have some bad news about your laptop charger. I took it with me to the library on Saturday and I think I left it there, because I've searched my bag and my room and I can't find it anywhere. I know you need it for your exam tomorrow morning, so I've already checked online, and the electronics shop near the station has the same model in stock. I'll buy a new one first thing when they open at eight and bring it straight to your place, and I'll also ask the library if anyone handed the old one in. Again, I'm really sorry for the stress.
samples.generationNotes: Top band: apology, clear explanation, acknowledges the exam, concrete and timely solution, appropriate tone for a classmate.

samples.transcript: The group discussed whether a four-day working week is a good idea.
